definitions.explanation: A highly prized wild mushroom that grows in association with pine trees. Known for its distinctive spicy-aromatic scent, it is considered a luxury food in Japan and is closely associated with autumn.

⟦{国産|こくさん}→国産：12017_kokusan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{松茸|まつたけ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{年々|ねんねん}→年々：10417_nennen⟧⟦{収穫量|しゅうかくりょう}→収穫量：29470_shuukakuryou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{減|へ}っていて→減る：01985_heru⟧、⟦{値段|ねだん}→値段：00871_nedan⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{高騰|こうとう}→高騰：14647_koutou⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Domestic matsutake yields have been declining year after year, and prices have been soaring.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
{松茸|まつたけ} is one of the most expensive mushrooms in the world. Domestic Japanese {松茸|まつたけ} can cost tens of thousands of yen per kilogram. It cannot be commercially cultivated and must be harvested from wild pine forests, which contributes to its high price and cultural prestige.

COMMON DISHES:
- {松茸|まつたけ}⟦ご{飯|はん}→ご飯：00776_gohan⟧: matsutake rice (rice cooked with matsutake)
- {松茸|まつたけ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{土瓶|どびん}⟦{蒸|む}し→蒸し：14266_mushi⟧: matsutake in an earthenware teapot broth
- ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧{松茸|まつたけ}: grilled matsutake

ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{松|まつ}→松：02256_matsu⟧ (pine) + {茸|たけ} (mushroom) — literally "pine mushroom," because it grows in symbiosis with pine tree roots.
